arxiv-1712-07198.title: Bose–Einstein correlations in \Pp ​ \Pp \Pp\Pp , \Pp \Pp Pb, and PbPb collisions at s NN = \sqrt{\smash[b]{s_{{}_{\text{NN}}}}}= 0.9–7 \TeV
arxiv-1712-07198.description: Abstract Quantum statistical (Bose–Einstein) two-particle correlations are measured in pp collisions at s = 0.9 \sqrt{s}=0.9 , 2.76, and 7 \TeV , as well as in \Pp \Pp Pb and peripheral PbPb collisions at nucleon-nucleon center-of-mass energies of 5.02 and 2.76 \TeV , respectively, using the CMS detector at the LHC.

arxiv-2010-15276.title: Ladder Operators and Hidden Algebras for Shape Invariant Nonseparable and Nondiagonalizable Models with Quadratic Complex Interaction. II. Three-Dimensional Model
arxiv-2010-15276.creator: Ian MARQUETTE a and Christiane QUESNE b
arxiv-2010-15276.description: Abstract A shape invariant nonseparable and nondiagonalizable three-dimensional model with quadratic complex interaction was introduced by Bardavelidze, Cannata, Ioffe, and Nishnianidze. However, the complete hidden symmetry algebra and the description of the associated states that form Jordan blocks remained to be studied.

arxiv-2103-09632.title: Inferred vs traditional personality assessment: are we predicting the same thing?
arxiv-2103-09632.creator: Pavel Novikov, Larisa Mararitsa, Victor Nozdrachev
arxiv-2103-09632.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Pavel Novikov, Larisa Mararitsa, Victor Nozdrachev. Machine learning methods are widely used by researchers to predict psychological characteristics from digital records. To answer whether automatic personality estimates retain the properties of the original traits, we reviewed 220 recent articles. First, we put together the predictive quality estimates from a subset of the studies which declare separation of training, validation, and testing phases, which is critical for ensuring the correctness of quality estimates in machine learning( Hastie et al.

arxiv-2103-12823.title: Thermal effects on the Casimir energy of a Lorentz-violating scalar in magnetic field
arxiv-2103-12823.creator: Andrea Erdas
arxiv-2103-12823.description: Abstract In this work I investigate the finite temperature Casimir effect due to a massive and charged scalar field that breaks Lorentz invariance in a CPT-even, aether-like way. I study the cases of Dirichlet and mixed (Dirichlet-Neumann) boundary conditions on a pair of parallel plates.

arxiv-2207-11771.title: Image Denoising Using Convolutional Autoencoder
arxiv-2207-11771.creator: Prashanth Venkataraman
arxiv-2207-11771.description: Abstract With the inexorable digitalisation of the modern world, every subset in the field of technology goes through major advancements constantly. One such subset is digital images which are ever so popular. Images can not always be as visually pleasing or clear as you would want them to be and are often distorted or obscured with noise.

arxiv-2309-09346.title: Speech-Gesture GAN: Gesture Generation for Robots and Embodied Agents
arxiv-2309-09346.creator: Carson Yu Liu, Gelareh Mohammadi, Yang Song, Wafa Johal
arxiv-2309-09346.description: Abstract Embodied agents, in the form of virtual agents or social robots, are rapidly becoming more widespread. In human-human interactions, humans use nonverbal behaviours to convey their attitudes, feelings, and intentions. Therefore, this capability is also required for embodied agents in order to enhance the quality and effectiveness of their interactions with humans.

arxiv-2406-19871.title: Koopman based trajectory model and computation offloading for high mobility paradigm in ISAC enabled IoT system
arxiv-2406-19871.creator: Minh-Tuan Tran
arxiv-2406-19871.description: Abstract User experience on mobile devices is constrained by limited battery capacity and processing power, but 6G technology advancements are diving rapidly into mobile technical evolution. Mobile edge computing (MEC) offers a solution, offloading computationally intensive tasks to edge cloud servers, reducing battery drain compared to local processing.

arxiv-2410-05509.title: An ADMM-Based Approach to Quadratically-Regularized Distributed Optimal Transport on Graphs
arxiv-2410-05509.creator: Yacine Mokhtari, Emmanuel Moulay, Patrick Coirault, Jerome Le Ny
arxiv-2410-05509.description: Abstract Optimal transport on a graph focuses on finding the most efficient way to transfer resources from one distribution to another while considering the graph’s structure. This paper introduces a new distributed algorithm that solves the optimal transport problem on directed, strongly connected graphs, unlike previous approaches which were limited to bipartite graphs.

arxiv-2501-03557.title: High-order synchronization in identical neurons with asymmetric pulse coupling
arxiv-2501-03557.creator: Abhay, Gaurav Dar
arxiv-2501-03557.description: Abstract The phenomenon of high-order ( p / q p/q ) synchronization, induced by two different frequencies in the system, is well-known and studied extensively in forced oscillators including neurons and to a lesser extent in coupled oscillators. Their frequencies are locked such that for every p p cycles of one oscillator there are q q cycles of the other.

arxiv-2504-02234.title: Position: LLM Social Simulations Are a Promising Research Method
arxiv-2504-02234.creator: Jacy R. Anthis, Ryan Liu, Sean M. Richardson, Austin C. Kozlowski, Bernard Koch, Erik Brynjolfsson, James Evans, Michael S. Bernstein
arxiv-2504-02234.description: Abstract Accurate and verifiable large language model (LLM) simulations of human research subjects promise an accessible data source for understanding human behavior and training new AI systems. However, results to date have been limited, and few social scientists have adopted this method.

arxiv-2504-13900.title: Supporting Students’ Reading and Cognition with AI Conference: Workshop on Tools for Thought; April 26, 2025; Yokohama, Japan CCS: Human-centered computing Empirical studies in HCI
arxiv-2504-13900.creator: Yue Fu, Alexis Hiniker
arxiv-2504-13900.description: Abstract . With the rapid adoption of AI tools in learning contexts, it is vital to understand how these systems shape users’ reading processes and cognitive engagement. We collected and analyzed text from 124 sessions with AI tools, in which students used these tools to support them as they read assigned readings for an undergraduate course.

arxiv-2507-14700.title: Corridor-based Adaptive Control Barrier & Lyapunov Functions for Safe Mobile Robot Navigation
arxiv-2507-14700.creator: Nicholas Mohammad, Nicola Bezzo
arxiv-2507-14700.description: Abstract Safe navigation in unknown and cluttered environments remains a challenging problem in robotics. Model Predictive Contour Control (MPCC) has shown promise for performant obstacle avoidance by enabling precise and agile trajectory tracking, however, existing methods lack formal safety assurances.

arxiv-2509-24464.title: Sinc basis set for molecular orbitals calculation of cavity in 1D
arxiv-2509-24464.creator: Xueyuan Yan
arxiv-2509-24464.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xueyuan Yan. We develop a numerical approach based on the sinc basis set for first-principles electronic structure calculations in one-dimensional systems. The method exploits the inherent accuracy and non-local character of the sinc functions to handle long-range couplings effectively. As a proof of principle, we provide a computational study of a molecule in an optical cavity, with our code directly calculating the emergence of the energy level splitting in the spectrum.

europmc-pmc3460881.title: Validation of reference genes for gene expression studies in virus-infected Nicotiana benthamiana using quantitative real-time PCR.
europmc-pmc3460881.creator: Liu D, Shi L, Han C, Yu J, Li D, Zhang Y.
europmc-pmc3460881.description: Nicotiana benthamiana is the most widely-used experimental host in plant virology. The recent release of the draft genome sequence for N. benthamiana consolidates its role as a model for plant-pathogen interactions. Quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) is commonly employed for...

pmc-10672223.title: Time-Restricted Eating and Its Metabolic Benefits
pmc-10672223.creator: Sneha Mishra, Patress A Persons, Andrea M Lorenzo, Swarna S Chaliki, Sophie Bersoux, Giovanni Abbate-daga
pmc-10672223.description: Newer management strategies are being evaluated to treat obesity, which continues to increase worldwide. After 12 h of fasting, the body switches from glucose to fat metabolism, regulating protein synthesis and autophagy. These cellular responses are central to the metabolic benefits of time-restricted eating (TRE), independent of calorie restriction and weight loss, and they have heightened interest in TRE regimens.

pmc-11284308.title: Diverging Relationships among Amyloid, Tau, and Brain Atrophy in Early-Onset and Late-Onset Alzheimer’s Disease
pmc-11284308.creator: Han Kyu Na, Jeong-Hyeon Shin, Sung-Woo Kim, Seongho Seo, Woo-Ram Kim, Jae Myeong Kang, Sang-Yoon Lee, Jaelim Cho, Justin Byun, Nobuyuki Okamura, Joon-Kyung Seong, Young Noh
pmc-11284308.description: PurposeAlzheimer’s disease (AD) dementia may not be a single disease entity. Early-onset AD (EOAD) and late-onset AD (LOAD) have been united under the same eponym of AD until now, but disentangling the heterogeneity according to the age of sonset has been a major tenet in the field of AD research.

pmc-11340026.title: Engineering Insights into Tailored Metal–Organic Frameworks for CO2 Capture in Industrial Processes
pmc-11340026.creator: Hamidreza Mahdavi, Alice Robin, Nathan T. Eden, Abdollah Khosravanian, Muhammad Munir Sadiq, Kristina Konstas, Stefan J. D. Smith, Xavier Mulet, Matthew R. Hill
pmc-11340026.description: Despite the known impacts on climate change of carbon dioxide emissions, the continued use of fossil fuels for energy generation leading to the emission of carbon dioxide (CO2) into the atmosphere is evident. Therefore, innovation to address and reduce CO2 emissions from industrial operations remains an urgent and crucial priority.

pmc-11655283.title: Improved characterization of 3′ single-cell RNA-seq libraries with paired-end avidity sequencing
pmc-11655283.creator: John T Chamberlin, Austin E Gillen, Aaron R Quinlan
pmc-11655283.description: Prevailing poly(dT)-primed 3′ single-cell RNA-seq protocols generate barcoded cDNA fragments containing the reverse transcriptase priming site or in principle the polyadenylation site. Direct sequencing across this site was historically difficult because of DNA sequencing errors induced by the homopolymeric primer at the ‘barcode’ end.

pmc-12371106.title: Leveraging sequences missing from the human genome to diagnose cancer
pmc-12371106.creator: Ilias Georgakopoulos-Soares, Ofer Yizhar-Barnea, Ioannis Mouratidis, Candace S Y Chan, Michail Patsakis, Akshatha Nayak, Rachael Bradley, Mayank Mahajan, Jasmine Sims, Dianne Laboy Cintron, Ryder Easterlin, Julia S Kim, Emmalyn Chen, Geovanni Pineda, Guillermo E Parada, John S Witte, Christopher A M
pmc-12371106.description: BackgroundCancer diagnosis using cell-free DNA (cfDNA) has the potential to improve treatment and survival but has several technical limitations.MethodsIn this study, we developed a prediction model based on neomers, DNA sequences 13–17 nucleotides in length that are predominantly absent from the genomes of healthy individuals and are created by tumor-associated mutations.

pmc-12394460.title: MYC target gene activation in chronic lymphocytic leukemia and richter transformation: links to aggressiveness and tumor microenvironment interactions
pmc-12394460.creator: M. Tsagiopoulou, S. Rashmi, M. Chatziaslani, I. Gut
pmc-12394460.description: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) is characterized by clinical and biological heterogeneity, with a subset of patients progressing to Richter Transformation (RT), an aggressive lymphoma. This study explores MYC target gene activation across various CLL stages and disease subgroups using bulk RNAseq and single-cell RNAseq data.

pmc-13100646.title: Serum Creatinine Clearance and Cognitive Function in Older Adults: Mediating Effects of Systemic Inflammatory Response Index
pmc-13100646.creator: Yuyao He, Wenyue Hu, Cheu Hiutung, Zhenyun Han
pmc-13100646.description: Background:The association between renal dysfunction and cognitive decline in older adults has been increasingly recognized, although the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study explored the association between serum creatinine clearance (Ccr) and cognitive function, and evaluated whether the Systemic Inflammatory Response Index (SIRI) mediates this relationship.

pmc-13268058.title: Financial Disparities in Microsurgical Reconstruction: Reimbursement Analysis of Head & Neck versus Breast Microsurgery
pmc-13268058.creator: Ashlie A. Elver, Adam B. Fleming, Matthew Sink, Laura S. Humphries, Benjamin C. McIntyre
pmc-13268058.description: ds, and experience prolonged postoperative courses. In contrast, free-flap breast reconstruction is typically elective, performed in healthier patients, and associated with shorter recoveries. This study compares provider and institutional reimbursement patterns between microsurgical domains to evaluate differences reflected in compensation.

pmc-13535097.title: Visual trait variation and allometric scaling indicate intra- and inter-caste plasticity in the social wasp Protopolybia sedula
pmc-13535097.creator: André Rodrigues de Souza, Priscila Araújo, Eduardo Fernando Santos, Fábio Santos do Nascimento, Amanda Prato, Wilson Franca, Emily Baird
pmc-13535097.description: Understanding how phenotypic plasticity arises in sensory traits is a key challenge in evolutionary and developmental biology. Eusocial insects offer a useful model for exploring it, because their castes perform distinct tasks and occupy different light environments. We examined morphological variation and scaling in the visual systems of female castes of Protopolybia sedula, a neotropical wasp with simultaneous polygyny.

pmc-13669624.title: UniProt data pruning and the growing invisibility of the dark proteome
pmc-13669624.creator: Ali Al-Fatlawi, Michael Schroeder
pmc-13669624.description: The protein resource UniProtKB has undergone a major, multi-stage reorganization of its protein space, implemented from release 2025_04 through release 2026_02. Analysis of UniProtKB and UniParc records accessed on 20 January 2026 showed that 125.9 million entries were last present in UniProtKB in 2025 and are now represented in UniParc, while ~200.
